purpose: Build the Water reasoning and language corpus that will guide OpenAI in explaining data-center water exposure, cooling-water accounting, local availability, competing uses, drought, disclosure quality, and infrastructure constraints without converting broad context into facility-level claims.

mission_boundary.academic_role: Academic works teach analytical language, reasoning structure, evidence calibration, and anti-pattern recognition. They are not runtime factual evidence.
mission_boundary.production_authority: AI Macro deterministic Water evidence remains the exclusive factual record supplied to OpenAI.
mission_boundary.domain_ownership: Water owns withdrawal, consumption, source, cooling design, local availability, drought exposure, competing demand, water and wastewater infrastructure, and disclosure quality. Power owns electricity demand and generation. Data Centers owns campus identity and development status.
mission_boundary.no_quality_discount: A national water-use context cannot substitute for facility evidence, and a mapped drought condition cannot establish campus supply, legal access, or operating risk.
mission_boundary.code_state: No production code is modified during acquisition. Integration occurs only after the completed corpus passes its integrity audit.

required_substantive_sections: framing, theory, or literature where present
audit_contract.journal_gate: Current Journal Impact Factor >= 2.0, used only as a binary gate and verified from an authoritative journal or publisher record.
audit_contract.whole_text_gate: Abstracts, snippets, metadata pages, previews, and partial text do not count as review or admission.
audit_contract.transfer_rule: A prior complete audit may be transferred only with its original provenance, exact bibliographic identity, current journal-gate verification, Water-specific bounded extraction, and explicit statement that it was not newly read.
audit_contract.rights_boundary: Store structured observations and provenance, not copied copyrighted passages.

batch_design.role: Data-center water, accounting, scarcity, cooling, energy-water nexus, and spatial foundation
Independent facility, cooling, and disclosure saturation challenge
Independent watershed, drought, competition, and infrastructure saturation challenge
Integrated local-realization and policy synthesis confirmation

audit_contract.saturation_rule: After the coverage map is complete, two consecutive independent five-source challenge batches must each add no more than two genuinely new universal families and reopen no material gap.
audit_contract.long_form_rule: Analyze two complete technical texts across approximately fourteen substantial passages, balanced between national water accounting and facility or watershed realization.
audit_contract.completion_rule: COMPLETE requires 30 unique qualifying admissions, complete rhetoric extraction, coverage of every production evidence job and boundary, two complete long-form texts, approximately fourteen passage analyses, demonstrated saturation, source/observation/family reconciliation, and machine validation.

evidence_targets: national crop-irrigation, thermoelectric-power, and public-supply withdrawals
facility records with direct water evidence
facility records with quantified withdrawal or consumption
mapped states with D2-or-worse drought area
mapped states with at least 25 percent D2-or-worse drought area
published data-center capacity in mapped drought-exposed states
relationship_chain: campus design and workload create a heat-rejection requirement
cooling architecture converts heat rejection into electricity and direct-water demand
electricity generation can add indirect water demand
water source and withdrawal determine gross intake
consumption and discharge determine net local water effects
watershed, utility, infrastructure, legal, seasonal, and competing-use conditions determine usable supply
disclosure quality determines what can be established publicly
hard_boundaries: Withdrawal, consumption, discharge, delivery, and replenishment are distinct.
Site water-use effectiveness is not a complete water footprint when electricity-generation water is material.
National or state water totals do not establish campus-level availability or scarcity.
State drought area is an exposure screen, not a facility outage, permit, price, aquifer, watershed, or utility-headroom measure.
Published data-center capacity is not water demand without operating state, utilization, cooling design, climate, and denominator.
Potable, surface, groundwater, reclaimed, recycled, and wastewater sources are not interchangeable.
Water volume and scarcity-weighted impact are distinct.
Thermoelectric water context cannot be added mechanically to facility water use because years, populations, system boundaries, and attribution differ.
A cooling technology can shift burdens among water, electricity, refrigerants, materials, waste heat, reliability, and cost.
A corporate target, restoration claim, or replenishment volume is not the same as reducing physical withdrawal or consumption at the exposed site.

measurement: withdrawal, consumption, discharge, delivery, and return flow
direct site water versus indirect electricity water
WUE, source-inclusive WUE, intensity, aggregate volume, and functional units
reported, modeled, estimated, allocated, and undisclosed quantities
facility, campus, utility, county, state, basin, watershed, and national denominators
facility_and_cooling: air, evaporative, chilled-water, liquid, immersion, hybrid, and economizer designs
heat load, IT utilization, climate, season, cycles of concentration, and blowdown
local_realization: water source, utility service, rights, permits, treatment, conveyance, and wastewater capacity
drought, scarcity, aquifer, streamflow, seasonality, and extreme-event exposure
competing municipal, agricultural, industrial, ecological, and power-sector uses
facility status, utilization, and temporal coincidence
reclaimed-water quality, infrastructure, reliability, and alternative-use constraints
decision_and_language: efficiency improvement versus aggregate demand growth
target, plan, contract, construction, operation, and verified outcome states
physical reduction versus procurement, offset, restoration, and replenishment

next_action: Build and screen a diverse candidate population; verify the seven transferred audits; complete eight new foundation audits; and issue the fifteen-source foundation checkpoint before beginning saturation challenges.
do_not_do: Do not narrate national water use as a data-center water estimate.
Do not treat drought exposure as site-level water unavailability.
Do not infer facility water demand from published electrical capacity alone.
Do not compare water figures across unlike boundaries or functional units.
Do not modify the production language layer until the Water corpus is complete and audited.
Do not label the corpus complete based on source count alone.
